html:
El Ghriba is a synagogue on the island of Djerba in southern Tunisia, home to one of the oldest Jewish communities in the Arab world. By tradition a synagogue has stood on the site for some 1,900 years; the present building is from the late 1800s.

Local legend says it was founded by priests fleeing the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem, with a stone from it. Each spring Jews from Tunisia, Israel and France come on pilgrimage. Djerba's Jews kept their own way of life when most Tunisian Jews left after 1948 and after independence (Jewish exodus from Arab lands).

In 2002 an al-Qaeda truck bomb killed about twenty people outside it, and in 2023 a guard shot dead several people during the pilgrimage. Djerba is also home to Ibadi Muslims. See also Judaism.
